title: Chapter 2: The Missing Hours
notes: Playable opening and nonclinical source-review continuation from revised Chapter 2 Scenes 01–02. Owner authorized Chapter 2 implementation; proposed dialogue remains pending narrative review. No new clinical findings, Mara interview, Ward Zero entry or supernatural effect. Work ownership is not clinical completion. The source-question review ends with an unresolved follow-up memo, not a received source packet or completed reconciliation. Both follow-up choices retain all missing information. No new exact event time or approved clinical fact is authored. Scene 04 (Voss institutional review) records factual scope, missing permissions and an authorized follow-up; the pending source request, credential audit and W0-B restriction are unchanged. An urgent safety escalation is feedback-only because no new clinical finding is documented. Scene 03 (Mara Ellis) is owner-approved (2026-10-18) and runs after Scene 04 in this build: clinical interview through the existing dialogue system, EHR note, then a separate referral of her date question to Records. No diagnosis, medication, forensic opinion or treatment effect; Mara is not an evidence source for the hospital inquiry. Scene 05 (working explanation) logs clock skew, migrated location codes, export sorting and identifier collision as untested candidate explanations and chooses one next check; every item stays open because no source packet has been received. Scene 06 (Hale's Door): Hale scopes the question and the player requests one permitted follow-up. No access, escort or inspection is granted; Ward Zero entry stays in Chapter 3. Scene 07 (An Incomplete Witness): a Facilities technician recalls hearing the old lift bell during a scheduled shutdown but did not see anyone use it. Recorded as witness memory only; no clue, evidence or anomaly is created. Scene 08 (The Door That Wasn't Left Open): an escorted inspection of the restricted lift lobby doors from the security corridor, lobby only. The doors are observed closed, then found ajar after the team looked elsewhere; the escort did not watch continuously. No entry, trapping, portal or anomaly. The pass is returned to Hale afterwards. Scene 09 (A File for the Wrong Day): two archived export representations disagree about the access-event date; time-zone provenance is unreconciled. The player places it in the authorized incident record (not Mara's clinical note) and chooses one handling: formal audit escalation, preserving the separate source versions, or independent technical review. Original files are never changed; Mara's note stays independent and confidential. Scene 10 (Missing Hours, closing beat): the analyst can account for part of the timing mismatch but not the whole interval, and the report says so. Bennett, ending her shift, closes the chapter. Chapter 2 completes with only audit inconsistencies, source disagreement, an unobserved door movement and uncertain witness recollection on record; no confirmed supernatural event, no Ward Zero entry. After Bennett leaves, an optional personal message arrives (partner, friend, family or the player's own reminder, or left until later); the choice is the player's moderate personal history and returns in Chapter 4's personal call. No patient or work detail is shared. The close is text only and then the chapter's owner-approved recap (static_gn_v1, opening on a black fade) plays; no exterior plate exists in the approved art, so no new environment is introduced.

objectives.text: Begin the new shift with Naomi at the nursing station.
Review the worklist at the handover board and retain clinical follow-up responsibility.
Compare the maintenance export in Records. Keep the discrepancy unresolved.
Request authorized source records from the office workstation.
Return to Naomi and acknowledge outstanding work.
Review the source-clock questions at the Records worksheet.
Review the repeated minute and export ordering in Records.
Check source independence at the office records-request workstation.
Track preservation and custody confirmation at the office workstation.
Scope the unresolved follow-up memo at the Records worksheet.
Return to Naomi and acknowledge the separate records and clinical follow-ups.
Meet Dr Voss privately and state only what the records establish.
With Dr Voss, identify the permissions the follow-up still needs and who owns them.
Agree an authorized follow-up with Dr Voss.
Interview Mara Ellis in Interview Room A: her records concern, sleep, mood history, alternatives, safety and collateral.
Document Mara's assessment in the EHR. Keep the records question out of the clinical formulation.
Send Mara's date question to Records from the office workstation, separately from her clinical record.
At the Records worksheet, go through the analyst's candidate explanations for the discrepancy.
Choose the next authorized check with the Records analyst.
Marcus Hale is waiting in the office. Ask him how the restricted designation appeared in a live request.
Ask Hale for one permitted follow-up.
A Facilities technician is at the interview room door. Ask what they actually noticed during the shutdown.
Decide how to follow up the technician's recollection.
Ask Marcus Hale whether the lift lobby can be inspected under escort.
Go through the ward entry doors with the escort and note the state of the lift lobby doors.
Check the lobby doors again and decide how to handle what you find.
Report back to Hale at the psychiatrist's office and return the escorted pass.
Records has flagged a file under the wrong day. Review it at the export comparison worksheet.
Decide how the conflicting export versions are handled.
The analyst has an answer on the timing. Hear it at the export comparison worksheet.
Nurse Bennett is ending her shift. Catch her before she goes.
Collect your things at the nursing station and head home.

staff_lines.text: Go home, Doctor. It'll still be unreconciled tomorrow.
Pass is back on my board. What you saw at the lobby is in the log as you wrote it.
Escort's waiting at the ward entry. Lobby doors only. Nothing past them.
I've told you what I heard. I didn't see anything, and I'd rather that's how it's written.
Security said you might want a word about the shutdown. I'll tell you what I can.
Your request is logged. Any inspection still needs authorization, Facilities, a safe route and a reason to enter. None of that is in place.
Doctor. Records said you'd have questions about W0-B. Ask them properly and I'll answer what I can.

Morning, Doctor. The W0-B access ticket is still with Information Security. The useful news is that we have patients to see. I can show you the reports, but do not take my summary as your examination. Keep the clinical work separate from the audit request.
The follow-up is in writing. Records still has your source request, Information Security has the credential question, and the clinical work stays with you and the nursing team.
Doctor. A private word, please, before this becomes a corridor rumour.
Morning, Doctor. Clinical work first. Once your records memo is with Naomi, come and find me.

interactions.title: Your phone
interactions.body: Your phone buzzes as you collect your things at the nursing station. Whatever it is, nothing from today's work goes into the reply: no patient, no record, no ward.

options.label: Reply with what happened on the ward today
options.response: You stop before you send it. A personal message is not the place for records, patients or the inquiry, and nothing from today is yours to share.

options.label: A message from your partner
options.response:
Partner: Long one? Call me when you're out. Dinner's waiting either way.

You: Leaving now. Can't talk about the day, but I'm glad you're there.

options.label: A message from a friend
options.response:
Friend: Still alive in there? Drinks this week, no shop talk.

You: Still alive. Drinks sound good. No shop talk is a promise.

options.label: A message from family
options.response:
Family: Just checking you got home all right. Ring when you can.

You: Heading home now. I'll ring tomorrow.

options.label: Your own reminder
options.response:
Reminder (set by you): Leave work at work. Write tomorrow's list, then stop.

You write three lines for tomorrow, then put the phone away.

options.label: Leave it for now
options.response: You put the phone in your pocket. It can wait until you're home.

interactions.unavailable_body: Nothing new on the board.

interactions.title: End of shift
interactions.body: You sign out at the staff entrance. The shift is over.

options.label: Head out
options.response:
You head home. The screen fades out.

[b]End of Chapter 2: The Missing Hours[/b]
On record: audit inconsistencies, source disagreement, an unobserved door movement and an uncertain witness recollection. W0-B remains locked; any inspection needs proper authorization.

interactions.unavailable_body: Nothing new on the board.

interactions.title: New-shift worklist
interactions.body: Clinical work remains the priority. Review the existing EHR and retain responsibility for outstanding assessment and follow-up. The administrative audit is a separate work item. This handoff does not replace examination or establish new findings.

options.label: Retain responsibility for clinical review and follow-up
options.response: You retain responsibility for the outstanding clinical review and follow-up. No clinical task is marked completed. The records discrepancy can be investigated separately.

interactions.unavailable_body: Begin the new shift with Naomi before accepting outstanding work.

interactions.title: Maintenance export comparison
interactions.body: Two representations of a maintenance entry display a four-minute discrepancy. One export repeats a minute. The raw time zone, clock source and sort order have not been verified. This is a reported records discrepancy; it does not establish missing time.

options.label: Record the discrepancy as unresolved
options.response: Comparison recorded as unresolved. Request the authorized source-system export and preservation of the originals before drawing conclusions.

interactions.unavailable_body: Confirm who owns the outstanding clinical review at the handover board before pursuing the audit.
interactions.completed_body: The initial mismatch is recorded as unresolved. Continue the source-clock review at this worksheet.

interactions.title: Authorized source request
interactions.body: Request preservation of the original records and an authorized source-system export. Ask for the raw offsets, clock source and sort order. Making a request does not grant access or authenticate a record.

options.label: Submit preservation and source-export request
options.response: Request submitted for authorized Records review. Source access and reconciliation remain pending. The originals must be retained; no independent corroboration or loss of time is established.

interactions.unavailable_body: Record the comparison as unresolved in Records before requesting source material.
interactions.completed_body: The preservation and export request is submitted. Receipt, custody and source independence still need verification.

interactions.title: New-shift handoff
interactions.body:
Bennett: We have patients to see. Keep the clinical work moving while Records checks the source material.

The audit request remains unresolved. You retain the outstanding clinical work.

options.label: Acknowledge the outstanding work and records follow-up
options.response: Handoff acknowledged. Clinical review remains assigned to you, and the source-export request remains with Records. Continue routine care while the source material is reconciled.

interactions.unavailable_body: The source request is not yet recorded. Clinical review remains separate from the audit.
interactions.completed_body: Clinical review remains assigned separately from the unresolved records inquiry.

interactions.title: Records worksheet: source clocks
interactions.body:
[b]Reported comparison[/b]
Two representations display a four-minute difference; an export repeats a minute.

[b]Available clock metadata[/b]
Raw time-zone offset: unverified.
Source clock and synchronization authority: unverified.
No authorized raw export has been received in this review.

What correction can this comparison support?

options.label: Apply a four-minute correction to reconcile the records
options.response: A displayed difference alone does not establish a clock correction. The source offsets and clock authority are still unverified. Retain the original representations and review the missing metadata.

options.label: Keep the correction unknown and request clock authority
options.response: Clock review recorded: no correction can be justified yet. Raw offsets, clock authority and synchronization history remain requested. The displayed mismatch remains unresolved.

interactions.unavailable_body: Complete the current records-review objective first. Clinical review remains a separate responsibility.
interactions.completed_body: Clock authority and raw offsets remain unverified. Continue with the export-order review at this worksheet.

interactions.title: Records worksheet: export order
interactions.body:
[b]Reported export[/b]
A minute appears more than once.

[b]Missing information[/b]
Raw event sequence, export sort key and transformation history have not been verified. A display row is not proof of an elapsed interval.

How should the repeated minute be recorded?

options.label: Classify the repeated minute as proven missing time
options.response: That conclusion exceeds the available source material. Repeated display values can only be recorded as a discrepancy while ordering and transformation history remain unverified.

options.label: Retain the repeated row and request raw ordering metadata
options.response: Export-order review recorded. Preserve the original representation and request its sort key, raw event sequence and transformation history. Do not reorder or overwrite the original.

interactions.unavailable_body: Complete the current records-review objective first. Clinical review remains a separate responsibility.
interactions.completed_body: Clock and export-order gaps are recorded. Review source dependencies at the office records-request workstation.

interactions.title: Source review: independence
interactions.body:
[b]Current material[/b]
The two displayed representations have not been traced to independently acquired originals. Source extraction, clock dependencies and transformation lineage remain unverified.

Would receiving another copy establish independent corroboration?

options.label: Count another copy as independent corroboration
options.response: A copy can preserve or reproduce a source; it does not by itself establish independence. Shared originals, clocks and export pipelines still need to be checked. No evidence status has been promoted.

options.label: Leave independence unestablished and request the source lineage
options.response: Dependency review recorded: source independence remains unestablished. Request original capture, clock authority, extraction history and shared dependencies before counting corroboration.

interactions.unavailable_body: Complete the current records-review objective first. Clinical review remains a separate responsibility.
interactions.completed_body: Source independence remains unestablished. Check the preservation request at this workstation.

interactions.title: Source review: preservation and custody
interactions.body:
[b]Request status[/b]
Preservation and an authorized source-system export have been requested.

[b]Outstanding confirmation[/b]
No original receipt, immutable checksum or custody acknowledgment is supplied by the current comparison. A request is not confirmation that preservation occurred.

How should the request be tracked?

options.label: Mark the originals as preserved because the request was sent
options.response: Sending the request does not confirm custody or preservation. Keep confirmation outstanding and retain the request without claiming receipt of an original.

options.label: Keep preservation confirmation and source receipt outstanding
options.response: Preservation follow-up recorded. Request confirmation of original receipt, unchanged source bytes/checksum and custody history from authorized Records staff. Receipt and preservation remain unconfirmed.

interactions.unavailable_body: Complete the current records-review objective first. Clinical review remains a separate responsibility.
interactions.completed_body: Preservation confirmation, raw export receipt and custody remain outstanding. Return to the Records worksheet to scope the follow-up memo.

interactions.title: Unresolved records memo
interactions.body:
[b]Reported[/b]
Four-minute displayed mismatch; repeated minute in an export.

[b]Still unknown[/b]
Clock authority and offsets; raw event ordering; extraction lineage and shared dependencies; original receipt, checksum and custody confirmation.

[b]Standing[/b]
Discrepancy unresolved. No proven loss of time, independent corroboration or patient finding. Preserve the original representations and keep clinical documentation separate.

Choose the emphasis for the next authorized follow-up. Both requests retain all outstanding source questions.

options.label: Prioritize clock authority and raw offsets in the follow-up
options.response: Unresolved memo recorded with clock-authority/offset verification prioritized. Records must also address ordering, lineage, custody and preservation. Source receipt and any reconciliation remain pending. Return to Naomi to acknowledge the outstanding work.

options.label: Prioritize source lineage and custody in the follow-up
options.response: Unresolved memo recorded with source-lineage/custody verification prioritized. Records must also address clock authority, offsets, ordering and preservation. Source receipt and any reconciliation remain pending. Return to Naomi to acknowledge the outstanding work.

interactions.unavailable_body: Complete the current records-review objective first. Clinical review remains a separate responsibility.
interactions.completed_body: The unresolved memo retains the reported mismatch and all missing source questions. An authorized technical follow-up is requested; original receipt, preservation and reconciliation remain pending. No independent corroboration or missing-time conclusion is recorded.

interactions.title: Records follow-up handoff
interactions.body:
Bennett: Keep the records questions with the authorized review. The clinical work still needs its own follow-up.

The comparison remains unresolved. Source receipt, clock verification and preservation confirmation remain outstanding. Your clinical responsibilities have not been marked completed by this inquiry.

options.label: Acknowledge the records follow-up and separate clinical responsibility
options.response: Records-review handoff acknowledged. The unresolved memo and authorized follow-up remain recorded. Continue clinical work separately; source material and technical reconciliation are still outstanding.

interactions.unavailable_body: Complete the current records-review objective first. Clinical review remains a separate responsibility.

interactions.title: Dr Voss: institutional review
interactions.body:
Voss steps aside where the corridor is quiet.

Voss: An incomplete entry can become an allegation very quickly. I'm not asking you to ignore it. I'm asking you to tell me what was actually established.

[b]On record[/b]
A transfer request to W0-B was logged under a staff credential marked inactive. The requester was not identified.
A four-minute displayed mismatch and a repeated minute in a maintenance export are recorded as unresolved. Your source request is pending with Records.

What do you tell her?

options.label: Say someone deliberately used the inactive credential
options.response: Voss: Who? The audit shows a credential, not a person. Write that someone did it on purpose and you have made an allegation the record does not support. Tell me what was established.

options.label: Say the export proves the ward lost four minutes
options.response: Voss: Records has not verified the clock source or the export order. A displayed mismatch is a discrepancy, not a missing interval. What do you actually have?

options.label: State only what is established, and what is not
options.response:
Player: An inactive credential appears in an archived transfer-request audit. It doesn't identify the person who used it. The export mismatch is reported and unresolved; clock authority, ordering, lineage and preservation are unverified.

Voss: Good. Document patient-safety concerns separately from information-security concerns. They have different owners.

Factual scope recorded. Talk to Voss again about what the follow-up still needs.

interactions.unavailable_body: Dr Voss wants the records memo acknowledged with Naomi first. Clinical work remains a separate responsibility.

interactions.title: Dr Voss: missing permissions
interactions.body:
Voss: Then separate the owners. What does the follow-up still need, and who has to authorize it?

[b]Factual scope[/b]
Inactive credential in a transfer-request audit; user not identified. Export discrepancy unresolved; source request pending with Records.

[b]Your current authority[/b]
Attending clinical access only. No credential-audit authority, no source-system access and no authorization for W0-B.

options.label: Ask Voss to authorize you to inspect W0-B yourself
options.response: Voss: No. W0-B is Security's door, and any inspection needs their authorization and an escort. A records question is not a reason to open a sealed ward. Your access is unchanged.

options.label: Ask for direct access to the raw source system
options.response: Voss: That isn't mine to hand out, and it shouldn't be yours to take. Records holds the source export; Information Security holds the credential audit. Your request stays with them.

options.label: Record the missing permissions and their owners
options.response:
Missing permissions recorded:
Information Security: audit of the inactive credential and who could use it.
Records: the pending preservation and source-export request, with clock and ordering metadata.
Security: any question about W0-B access policy. No inspection is authorized.
Clinical follow-up stays with you and the nursing team.

Voss: That is a list I can send to people who can act on it. Now tell me what you want to happen next.

interactions.unavailable_body: Dr Voss wants the records memo acknowledged with Naomi first. Clinical work remains a separate responsibility.

interactions.title: Dr Voss: authorized follow-up
interactions.body:
Voss: What do you want to happen next? Pick something I can authorize today.

[b]Still pending[/b]
Records source request, preservation confirmation and reconciliation. Information Security credential audit. No new clinical finding has been documented in this review.

options.label: Press for an urgent patient-safety escalation
options.response: Voss: On what finding? Nothing in this review documents a new risk to a patient. If your clinical assessment identifies one, escalate it through clinical channels at once and I will back you. It does not ride on an audit memo. Choose a follow-up the record supports.

options.label: Request the written escalation process
options.response:
Voss: Reasonable. I'll send you the incident-escalation procedure and copy the Records and Information Security leads. Your source request stays open with Records; nothing is closed by this.

Follow-up recorded: written process requested. The records discrepancy and the credential audit remain unresolved.

options.label: Propose an independent records reconciliation
options.response:
Voss: I'd rather Records finished its own work first. But a neutral second review is a fair request, and I'll put it to the quality committee in writing. It does not replace your pending request.

Follow-up recorded: independent reconciliation proposed. The source request, preservation confirmation and credential audit remain pending.

interactions.unavailable_body: Dr Voss wants the records memo acknowledged with Naomi first. Clinical work remains a separate responsibility.

interactions.title: Records referral: Mara Ellis's question
interactions.body:
[b]Request[/b]
Mara Ellis asks for two copies of her aunt Lillian Ellis's 1988 record to be checked: a paper record dated October 12 and a later archive copy dated October 14.

[b]Separation[/b]
This is an administrative records question. It is not part of the hospital's W0-B inquiry, and Mara's clinical assessment stays in the EHR.

How should it be sent?

options.label: Attach your clinical assessment to support her request
options.response: Records does not need her clinical details to compare two copies. Send only what the question requires; her assessment stays confidential in the EHR.

options.label: Add the date conflict to the W0-B records inquiry
options.response: Mara is a patient with her own question, not a source for the hospital's inquiry. Nothing links her aunt's record to W0-B. Refer it on its own.

options.label: Refer the date question to Records on its own
options.response: Referral sent to the authorized Records office: two copies, two dates, origin of each copy to be checked. No finding about the records is made, and nothing in Mara's clinical assessment changes. Her follow-up (sleep and function support, safety follow-up, legal-role clarification, medication reconciliation) stays with the clinical team.

interactions.unavailable_body: Document Mara's assessment in the EHR first. Her records question is referred separately.
interactions.completed_body: Mara's date question is with Records, separate from her clinical record. No finding about the copies has been made.

interactions.title: Records analyst: candidate explanations
interactions.body:
The Records analyst has the worksheet open.

Analyst: The familiar explanations aren't glamorous. They're also where we have to start.

[b]Candidates[/b]
Clock skew between the console and the export: could explain the four-minute display difference.
Migrated location codes: could explain why an entry is labelled with an old designation.
Export sorting: could explain the repeated minute.
Identifier collision: could explain an entry attached to the wrong record.

[b]Status[/b]
None has been tested against source material; no source packet has been received.

Player: And when they don't account for every line?

options.label: Accept clock skew as the explanation for the whole discrepancy
options.response: Analyst: Skew might cover the four minutes. It doesn't touch the repeated row, and we haven't checked a single source clock yet. One candidate isn't an answer.

options.label: Treat whatever stays unexplained as proven altered time
options.response: Analyst: Unexplained means unexplained. Contradictory timestamps are a records problem until a source shows otherwise. That isn't evidence of anything else.

options.label: Log all four as untested candidates and keep the mismatch open
options.response:
Analyst: We preserve the mismatch and keep checking.

Candidates logged: clock skew, migrated location codes, export sorting, identifier collision. Each may explain part of the discrepancy; none is confirmed. The discrepancy stays unresolved.

interactions.unavailable_body: Complete the current objective first. The records discrepancy remains unresolved.
interactions.completed_body: Four candidate explanations are logged as untested. Choose the next check with the analyst at this worksheet.

interactions.title: Records analyst: next check
interactions.body:
Analyst: I can start one of these properly this week. Which first?

[b]Still open[/b]
All four candidates; clock authority and offsets; raw ordering; source lineage; preservation confirmation.

options.label: Close the discrepancy as a migration artefact
options.response: Analyst: Not on what we have. A migration might explain the label, not the timing. Closing it now would be deciding the answer first.

options.label: Request a source extraction of the original console log
options.response: Next check recorded: source extraction requested through Records' authorized process. It tests clock skew and export sorting once received. Nothing is received yet; every candidate stays open.

options.label: Build an identifier crosswalk between the old and current systems
options.response: Next check recorded: identifier crosswalk between legacy and current codes. It tests migrated location codes and identifier collision. Clock and ordering questions stay open.

options.label: Request a neutral second review of the worksheet
options.response: Next check recorded: neutral second review requested. A reviewer outside the team re-checks the candidates and the method. No candidate is confirmed in the meantime.

interactions.unavailable_body: Log the candidate explanations first.
interactions.completed_body: The next check is recorded. The discrepancy and all four candidate explanations remain open until source material is received and reviewed.

interactions.title: Marcus Hale: the restricted designation
interactions.body:
Hale: The historical label isn't an operational ward assignment. And the clinical transfer system isn't the security badge system.

What do you ask him?

options.label: Ask for a badge so you can look at W0-B yourself
options.response: Hale: That door has a control list. Curiosity isn't on it. Your access is unchanged.

options.label: Say the transfer request proves someone opened W0-B
options.response: Hale: A request in the transfer system isn't a door event. Nothing you've shown me says that door opened. Ask me what you actually need to know.

options.label: Ask how the restricted designation appeared in a live request
options.response:
Player: I'm asking how the restricted designation appeared in a live request.

Hale: Appropriate question. The answer needs an authorized audit, not an unauthorized inspection.

Player: What would a legitimate inspection require?

Hale: Authorization, Facilities, a safe route, and a reason to enter.

Question recorded. Ask Hale for one permitted follow-up.

interactions.unavailable_body: Hale is not here yet.

interactions.title: Marcus Hale: permitted follow-up
interactions.body:
Hale: I can do one of these without anyone breaking policy. Pick.

[b]Not available[/b]
Badge access, escort or inspection of W0-B. No authorization exists.

options.label: Ask Hale to escort you into W0-B today
options.response: Hale: No. Not today and not on my word alone. An inspection needs authorization, Facilities and a safe route first. Choose something I can actually do.

options.label: Request a clinical risk check on the transfer request
options.response:
Hale: Security won't act on a transfer to a non-operational designation while the audit runs. Whether the request put a patient at risk is a clinical question; that review is yours.

Follow-up recorded: clinical risk check requested. No patient is moved and no access changes.

options.label: Ask for a permitted summary of the access-log report
options.response:
Hale: You'll get the summary the policy allows: what was logged and when, not the raw badge data. It won't name anyone the audit hasn't.

Follow-up recorded: permitted report summary requested. The credential audit stays with Information Security.

options.label: Ask about archived facilities plans for the historic wing
options.response:
Hale: Facilities keeps those. I'll ask them to release what's archived to you through Records. Plans aren't permission to go anywhere.

Follow-up recorded: archived facilities plans requested. No route or access is authorized.

interactions.unavailable_body: Ask Hale about the designation first.

interactions.title: Facilities technician: the shutdown
interactions.body:
Technician: I heard the old lift bell. Could've been the test cycle. Sound carries strangely through the pipes.

What do you ask?

options.label: "So someone took the old lift down during the shutdown?"
options.response:
Technician: I didn't say that. I heard a bell. If you write it that way you're writing something I never saw.

That question suggested an answer. Ask it again without one.

options.label: "Did you actually see anyone use the elevator?"
options.response:
Technician: No. I wouldn't say I did.

Recorded as reported: heard what sounded like the old lift bell during a scheduled shutdown; possibly the test cycle; did not see anyone use the lift. This is witness memory, not an observation of movement.

interactions.unavailable_body: The technician is busy.

interactions.title: Facilities technician: follow-up
interactions.body:
Technician: Anything else? I've got closers to finish.

[b]On record[/b]
Heard a bell during a scheduled shutdown; did not see the lift used; timing not checked.

options.label: Record that the lift moved during the shutdown
options.response: Nobody saw the lift move. A remembered bell can't be written up as movement. Choose a follow-up that checks it.

options.label: Ask which work orders covered the shutdown and test cycle
options.response:
Technician: Facilities logs every test cycle. I'll send you the work-order numbers for that shift.

Follow-up recorded: confirm scheduled work orders. The bell may match a test; nothing is concluded yet.

options.label: Keep the recollection exactly as reported, with its uncertainty
options.response: Follow-up recorded: the statement stands in the technician's own words, including "could've been the test cycle" and "I wouldn't say I did". No inference is added.

options.label: Ask when they heard it, without suggesting a time
options.response:
Technician: Late in the shift. I didn't look at a clock.

Follow-up recorded: timing to be checked against shift and work-order records. No time is assigned from memory.

interactions.unavailable_body: Ask what the technician noticed first.

interactions.title: Marcus Hale: escorted inspection
interactions.body: Hale: You want eyes on the lift lobby. I can send an escort to the lobby doors with you. Not into the lobby, not the lift, not the hatch, and nowhere near W0-B.

options.label: Ask to continue down to W0-B if the lobby looks clear
options.response: Hale: No. There's no authorization, no Facilities sign-off and no clinical reason to enter. The pass covers the lobby doors and nothing past them.

options.label: Accept an escorted look at the lobby doors only
options.response:
Hale: Escorted pass logged against this inspection. The ward entry doors will open for you. Bring the pass back to me when you're done.

Scope recorded: lobby doors only, with an escort. Lift, service hatch and W0-B remain locked.

interactions.unavailable_body: Hale is busy.

interactions.title: Restricted lift lobby doors
interactions.body:
The double doors to the restricted lift lobby are shut. The latch is engaged and the reader shows locked.

The escort stands beside you.

options.label: Try the doors
options.response:
Escort: Not on this pass, Doctor. We look; we don't go in.

The doors stay shut.

options.label: Note the time and that the doors are closed and latched
options.response:
Noted: lobby doors closed, latch engaged, reader locked.

The escort's radio goes. Facilities wants the maintenance door checked. You both step along the corridor to look at it, and for a minute neither of you is watching the lobby.

interactions.unavailable_body: The lobby doors are behind the ward entry. You have no reason or pass to inspect them.

interactions.title: Restricted lift lobby doors
interactions.body:
When you turn back, the right-hand lobby door stands ajar by a few centimetres. Nobody passed you in the corridor that you saw.

Escort: Someone could have used the maintenance route.

You: Then let's check the approved work orders before concluding anything.

The escort did not watch the doors continuously, and neither did you.

options.label: Step into the lobby to see who is there
options.response:
Escort: Not on this pass. If someone's in there, Security handles it.

You stay in the corridor.

options.label: Record that someone opened the doors while you were away
options.response: Nobody saw the doors opened. A latch that failed, a pressure change or a person are all possible. Record what was observed, not who did it.

options.label: Document the state: closed and latched, then ajar, with the unwatched interval
options.response: Documented: doors closed and latched at first check; ajar on return; the escort and you did not watch them continuously in between. No cause is recorded.

options.label: Have the escort secure the doors and report it under policy
options.response:
Escort: Closing them now and calling it in.

The doors are pushed shut and the latch engages. Security has the report: found ajar during an escorted check, cause unknown.

options.label: Request a latch and ventilation assessment from Facilities
options.response: Request recorded: Facilities to check the lobby door latch and the corridor ventilation pressure. The doors were found ajar after an unwatched interval; no cause is assumed.

interactions.unavailable_body: Note the doors' state first.
interactions.completed_body: Lobby doors: observation and follow-up recorded. Return the pass to Hale.

interactions.title: Marcus Hale: lobby report
interactions.body: Hale: Well?

options.label: Ask to keep the pass for a follow-up visit
options.response: Hale: The pass was for one inspection. Any follow-up gets its own request.

options.label: Report what you recorded and return the escorted pass
options.response:
Hale reads your note and signs the pass back in.

Hale: Closed, then ajar, nobody watching in between. That's what goes in the log.

The ward entry doors are controlled access again.

interactions.unavailable_body: Hale is busy.

interactions.title: A file for the wrong day
interactions.body:
Two archived export representations of the same access event disagree about its date. The time-zone provenance of each is still being reconciled. Neither version is shown to be the original.

Mara Ellis also raised a date question about her records. Where does this belong?

options.label: Add it to Mara's clinical note as context for her concern
options.response: Her note documents her care. An export date conflict is not a clinical finding and does not belong in her record. Her note stays as written and confidential.

options.label: Treat the conflict as part of her presentation
options.response: A disagreement between two system exports is not a psychiatric symptom. Nothing about it is hers.

options.label: "This isn't a psychiatric symptom. It belongs in the authorized incident record."
options.response:
Records technician: Then we preserve the original versions as they were received.

Recorded in the incident record: two export representations disagree on the access-event date; time-zone provenance unreconciled. Mara's clinical note is unchanged and kept separate.

interactions.unavailable_body: Nothing new at the worksheet yet.

interactions.title: A file for the wrong day: handling
interactions.body:
[b]Incident record[/b]
Two export versions; dates disagree; time-zone provenance unreconciled; originals as received.

How should it be handled?

options.label: Correct one version so the dates match
options.response:
Records technician: We don't edit originals. A corrected copy would be a third version, not an answer.

Nothing is changed.

options.label: Request formal audit escalation
options.response: Escalation requested through the audit process. Both versions stay as received; no date is chosen.

options.label: Preserve the separate source versions as received
options.response: Both versions are preserved separately with their provenance. Neither is treated as corroborating the other.

options.label: Request independent technical review of the time-zone handling
options.response: Independent technical review requested. Until it reports, the date stays unresolved.

interactions.unavailable_body: Decide where the date conflict belongs first.
interactions.completed_body: Incident record: two export versions disagree on the date; handling recorded; originals unchanged.

interactions.title: Missing hours
interactions.body:
The analyst's note is attached to the worksheet.

Analyst: I can show you where the clocks differ. I can't reconstruct this interval responsibly from these records alone.

Part of the mismatch is accounted for by clock differences between systems. The rest of the reported interval is not.

options.label: Report the whole interval as clock skew
options.response: The analyst only accounts for part of it. Writing the rest off as skew claims more than the records show.

options.label: Report the remainder as missing time
options.response: Unreconciled is not missing. The records don't establish that any time was lost; they establish that they can't be reconciled yet.

options.label: "Then the report should say that."
options.response: Report recorded: part of the timing mismatch is explained by clock differences; the remainder of the reported interval cannot be reconstructed from the available records. Source, preservation and audit requests remain open.

interactions.unavailable_body: Nothing new at the worksheet yet.

interactions.title: Nurse Bennett: end of shift
interactions.body:
Bennett is pulling on her coat.

Bennett: Any luck?

options.label: "We found the missing hours."
options.response:
Bennett: Did you? Or did you find records that don't agree?

You haven't found anything that was lost. Tell her what you actually have.

options.label: "We confirmed there are records we can't reconcile yet."
options.response:
Bennett: Then you're doing what you're supposed to. Don't decide the answer first.

She heads for the staff entrance.

interactions.unavailable_body: Bennett is busy.

sign_out.title: Clinical handoff
sign_out.undocumented_message: Outstanding clinical review still requires an appropriate handoff.
